subject: Re: Data residency & region pinning - Acme Bank
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmebank.com>, Bob Lee <bob.lee@acmebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Data residency & region pinning

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we’re all aligned:

Summary of the ask:
- Acme wants EU-only processing for production traffic (APAC/US only for dev/test).
- No cross-region replication for PII; backups and snapshots must remain in EU.
- Audit logs to be retained for 12 months and available for export to customer SIEM.
- Customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest is required.

What we heard and noted:
- Primary production region: eu-west-1 (Ireland)
- RPO/RTO expectations: low RTO (preferably < 30 min), but any cross-region failover must not replicate PII outside EU without explicit approval.
- Retention: 12 months for logs, 90 days default for model-derived artifacts unless Acme requests longer for auditability.

Open questions for Acme (please confirm):
1) Do you require cross-region failover at all times, or would a manual DR runbook suffice to avoid automatic replication of PII?
2) For backups: must snapshots be geo-fenced to EU at all layers (application, object storage, DB)?
3) Any specific compliance evidence (e.g., CSV mapping of where PII fields originate) you want included in our SOC2 packet?

What we can provide now:
- Redwood supports per-tenant region pinning. We can pin production to eu-west-1.
- Backups and snapshots can be scoped to remain in the same region; cross-region replication is configurable and can be disabled.
- Customer-managed KMS is supported (bring-your-own-key).
- Audit logs can be retained for 12 months and streamed to your SIEM or delivered via secure S3 link.

Attachments: I’m including a short whitepaper on region pinning and a SOC2 evidence checklist (see attachments).

Next steps:
- Alice: confirm answers to the 3 questions above and confirm whether you want automatic failover or manual DR.
- Aditya: can you validate the technical constraints for per-tenant backup scoping and KMS notes so we can confirm SLA impacts?
- I’ll schedule a technical deep-dive next week (30–45 min) to walk through the architecture and a proposed runbook.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Sean
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmebank.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Data residency & region pinning

Thanks Sean — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our security/compliance side: 

- We require EU-only processing for all production data containing PII. Development and non-PII test data can be processed in other regions.
- Backups (including automated snapshots and DR replicas) must be stored within the EU. No synchronous replication of PII to non-EU regions is permitted.
- Audit logs: retention 12 months is acceptable. We also want the ability to export logs on demand (S3 or SIEM pull).
- KMS: we need BYOK with keys rented/managed in our tenant and key control in our KMS (Azure Key Vault).

Q: For the RTO/RPO you documented — if automatic failover would cause any PII to move outside the EU, we will not allow automatic failover. We can consider a warm-standby in EU if that’s possible.

Also attaching the internal compliance checklist for this evaluation (small excerpt). Would appreciate your engineering team’s confirmation on the BYOK integration and a simple diagram of the region failover behavior.

— Alice
Director, Cloud Security | Acme Bank
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmebank.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Data residency & region pinning

Hi Alice — thanks for the clarifications. Quick technical notes (TL;DR: everything you asked for is supported; a couple of configuration tradeoffs to confirm):

1) Region pinning and backups
- Redwood supports tenant-level region pinning (we can pin production to eu-west-1).
- Backups/snapshots can be configured to never leave the pinned region. Cross-region replication is off by default for tenants that opt into strict residency.
- Warm-standby in EU: we can provision a hot or warm standby cluster in a second EU AZ or another EU region. For warm-standby, snapshots remain in eu regions only and are only mounted after a manual or orchestrated DR event (no automated replication of PII).

2) Cross-region failover and PII
- Automatic failover is possible but only if configured to a target within EU. If a failover target is outside EU, we will not enable automatic failover for PII-tagged tenants. We can implement a manual failover runbook to meet your control requirements.

3) KMS / Encryption
- BYOK is supported. We integrate with customer-managed KMS (Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS, GCP KMS) via external key wrapping and access policies. Keys remain under your control; Redwood does not store plaintext keys.

4) Logging and audit retention
- Audit logs can be retained for 12 months in an EU region and streamed to your SIEM (via secure VPN/VPC peering or S3 export).
- We can provide periodic snapshots of audit logs or adhoc exports for audits.

5) SLA and operational impact
- If we disable cross-region replication and require manual DR, the platform’s RTO increases (we estimate 30–120 minutes depending on dataset size and snapshot restore time). If you need sub-10 minute RTO, that requires synchronous replication which would replicate metadata only; full PII replication to another EU region would be required for that SLA.

I’ve attached our region pinning whitepaper and SOC2 evidence checklist. Happy to run through a diagram in the deep-dive.

— Aditya
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Alice — this is great and exactly the level of detail we needed. Quick summary and proposed next steps: 

- Confirmed: EU-only processing for production PII; backups/snapshots geo-fenced to EU.
- Control model: BYOK (Azure Key Vault) supported.
- Failover: we will not enable automatic cross-region failover that moves PII outside the EU. Proposed approach: configure warm-standby in a secondary EU AZ/region + manual DR runbook.
- SLA note: with manual DR and no cross-region PII replication, expected RTO 30–120 min (we’ll provide runbook recovery time estimates based on dataset sizes in the deep-dive).

Action items:
1) Alice/Acme: confirm you are ok with warm-standby + manual DR (yes/no) and confirm the required SLA target if different from our estimates.
2) Acme security: share any additional SOC2 evidence mapping you want included (Alice — you mentioned an excerpt).
3) Redwood (Aditya + Marissa): prepare a short architecture diagram and a proposed DR runbook + time estimates.
4) Sean: I’ll send a calendar invite for a 30–45 min technical deep-dive next Tue/Wed (proposed times in invite).

If that all looks good I’ll convert this into the next-step joint MPA (mutual action plan) and attach to HubSpot.

Thanks again — talk soon.

Best,
Sean
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
